# ASCII art skill — and the page rules that override it

This is a general ASCII art skill. Drawing comic pages in this room, these rules win
wherever the skill says otherwise:

- **Canvas.** The page is a fixed 116 x 82 grid (one cell = one lettered letter). Ignore the
  skill's 72-column limit; return exactly the skeleton's size.
- **Text characters are for text only.** Letters, digits and `. , ! ? ' " - : ;` appear only
  in lettering. Where the skill draws with them, substitute: `.` and `,` -> `_` or `` ` ``;
  `'` -> `` ` ``; `-` -> `=` or `~`; `:` `;` `!` -> `|`; `o` `O` `0` -> `@` or `*`;
  `v` `V` -> `^`; letters used as texture -> `#` `%` `&` `@` `$`. Eyes are `*` or `@`.
- **Fonts.** Pages render in one known monospace font, so `^ ~ * #` are safe and useful —
  ignore the skill's warning about them.
- **No signatures or credits** on pages, and draw original work only.
- Emoticons, banners, Unicode and animation sections don't apply to pages.

---

ASCII art

You are drawing on a grid of monospaced cells. Each character is a fixed tile with a shape and a visual weight; the art is choosing which tile goes in which cell so that the eye connects them into lines that are not really there. Everything below follows from that.

Hard rules (never break)
Use only printable ASCII (codes 32 to 126) unless the user asks for Unicode. Never use tabs or control characters. Every gap is literal spaces.
Output the art inside a fenced code block with the text language tag so whitespace is preserved. Keep every line at or under 72 columns (80 if the user allows). Never let a line wrap.
Design for a cell that is about twice as tall as it is wide. A square needs roughly twice as many columns as rows. / and \ are steep; long gentle slopes are made by stepping with \_, -, . and ' between diagonals.
Draw original work. If you reproduce a known piece, keep the artist's initials exactly where they are and name the artist. Never sign someone else's work and never invent a credit; say "artist unknown" if it is unknown. You may sign your own work with a short tag if the user wants one.
Do not rely on characters whose glyph moves between fonts for structural alignment: ' \* ^ ~ I #. Use | not I for vertical bars.
Workflow

Do these steps in order. For anything larger than a one liner, draft on scratch paper (a code block you revise) before presenting the final.

1. Decide size band from the request and context.

Tiny (1 to 3 lines, under 12 chars): every character is a pictogram. Choose symbols, do not draw lines. Best for chat, signatures, inline use.
Small (4 to 8 lines): silhouette outline plus one or two features. Default for "draw me a cat".
Medium (9 to 20 lines): real line drawing with curves, some texture, a ground line, props.
Large (20+ lines): composition and shading. Only when asked for detail or a scene.

2. Pick a subject silhouette. Things with a recognizable outline work (cat, owl, fish, car, house, tree, rocket, dragon). Reduce the subject to two or three masses and note where the ground is.

3. Block in the silhouette with a few marks (/\ ears, \_ ground, . at each turn of the outline). Squint test: if the silhouette does not read, detail will not save it.

4. Draw the outline one row at a time. For each cell, choose the character whose stroke continues the line entering that cell. The end of a stroke must be adjacent (including diagonally) to the start of the next: \ ends bottom right, so the next row's stroke starts one column to the right. Curves are chains of one row steps (_.-', `-._), never jumps of two rows.

5. Place features. Eyes, mouth, wheels, windows are single characters or pairs placed in the right cells. Symmetric features go on symmetric columns; count columns from the outline to check. Leave more empty space than feels necessary.

6. Hint. Remove every stroke the eye can supply. A back can be one \_; a car's underside can be missing if the wheels are there; a fence is |^|^|. Cover parts of the drawing mentally; whatever is still recognizable without a stroke does not need it.

7. Verify before output. Check column by column: no tabs, no line over the width limit, symmetric parts on the same columns, boxes closed, every row of a frame the same length, no accidental trailing characters. Then present it.

Palette

Straight lines: \_ (baseline), - (middle), " ~ ^ (top), = (heavy), | (vertical), ! (vertical with a gap, good for legs), : ; (light vertical), / \ (steep diagonals). V v A X Y W M w pack diagonals into one cell.

Curves (all hinted): ( ) sides of round things; . , bottom of a curve; ' ` top of a curve; { } < > sharper bows. Core joints, memorize them:

text
.-. .--. _.-' `-._ .' `.      ,'   `.
( ) / \ / \ ' `
 `-' \ /
`--'

.-. over `-' is a circle. .' climbs right, '. descends right. _.-' flattens out to the right, `-.\_ to the left. ,| and |' round off corners.

Corners: + for technical boxes; . (top) and ' (bottom) for soft boxes; / \ for things that widen downward; < > cap horizontal ends (beaks, arrowheads, tails); ( ) cap vertical ends (feet, paws, lids).

Weight ramp, light to dark, for shading: .:-=+_#%@ (short) or .'^",:;Il!i~+\_-?][}{1)(|/tfjrxnuvczXYUJCLQ0OZmwqpdbkhao_#MW&8%B@$(long). In shaded work choose by weight and ignore shape; in line work the reverse.b d p q g 6 9` add weight on one side of a cell only (eyes, cheeks, highlights).

Specialists: o O 0 @ \* eyes, wheels, suns, stars; w v Y T noses and mouths; ~ water, smoke, whiskers, tails; ^ ears, waves, grass, peaks; % & foliage; # mesh, brick, hedgehogs; 8 round dense things; $ money and dense fill; Z sleep.

Reusable constructions

Cat head: /\_/\ then ( o.o ) then > ^ <. Cat with whiskers in one line: =^..^=. Owl: /\ /\ over ((ovo)) over ():::() over VVV. Bird: ^V^ or ('v'); side view >' ). Fish: ><>, ><(((\*>, <`)))))<. Dog side view: ear ( or ^, tail / or ~, legs || ||. Sleeping: zzZ or ZZZzz above the head.

Wheels: (_), ( ), (o); undercarriage `-(_)--(_)-'. Windows: [], [_], |_|. Simple house: roof /\ widened over rows, walls | |, door |_|, window [].

Ground lines: **\_\_** floor, ~~~~~~ water, ^^^^^^ grass, ,,,,,, short grass, "" "" paw prints, ----- road, =-=-=- tracks, ~^~^~^ waves.

Sky: sparse \* . ' for stars; moon ( alone or \_/ over -=(_)=- for a sun; clouds .-. ( ) `-' or _.-~-.\_.

Feet: (_), _/, \_, '-', m m, "" "". Tails: ~, ), _.-', `-._.

Shadow: same outline shifted one column right and one row down in . and :. Depth: near objects larger and heavier (# | @), far objects smaller and lighter (. ' ``), near overwrites far.

Emoticons and kaomoji

Sideways (Western): eyes : ; 8 B =, optional nose - o ^, mouth ) ( D P O / | _. Examples: :-) ;-) :-( :-_ :-P 8-) :-o.

Upright (kaomoji): brackets ( ) [ ] { } < > around eyes and mouth; arms outside. Eyes: ^ ^ happy, o o O O surprised, - - calm or asleep, > < squint, @ @ dizzy, x x dead, \* \* excited, T T crying, ; ; sweating. Mouths: _ neutral, o singing, . small, w cat, 3 kiss, ~ drool. Arms: \( )/ cheer, <( )> stance, d( )b headphones, t( )t rude. Examples: (^_^), (-_-)zzz, (>'.')><('.'<) hug, \(^-^)/, (#^.^#) shy, @_@ dizzy, ¯\_(ツ)\_/¯ shrug (needs Unicode).

Rule for tiny work: remove any character whose removal leaves the thing recognizable; symmetry is free identity.

Lettering and banners

Draw each letter as a five or six row outline in \_ | / \ ( ) ' . on a shared baseline with one consistent height and stroke vocabulary (FIGlet "standard" look). Adjacent letters may share an edge column. Example, the word "cats":

text
\_
**\_ ** _| |_ **\_
/ **/ _` | **/ **|
| (_| (_| | |_\_\_ \
 \_**\__,_|\__|_**/

For a heavier, foolproof banner use block letters: each letter five rows high, about five wide, made of a repeated character (# or the letter itself). Keep banners at or under 72 columns; break long words into two banners rather than shrinking.

Borders, dividers, patterns

Box: corners + with - and |, or ./' corners for a soft look. Every row must be the same length; the top and bottom rows must be identical in length to each other and the inner rows must have the same total width.

text
+----------+ .----------. ╔══════════╗ (Unicode only)
| | | | ║ ║
+----------+ '----------' ╚══════════╝

3D box: draw the box, then add a second right edge of | one column right and a bottom edge of _ one row down, joined with / at the corners. Divider: a two to four character unit tiled to the width, ending on a whole unit (-=-=-=, ~^~^~^, <><><>, +-+-+-, O()O(), _.".\_."). Two row dividers use a unit spanning rows (/\_/\_ over \/ \/). Pattern: a divider extended down, rows either in phase (grid) or shifted (brick or diamond).

Shading and texture

Tone: five or six weights at most, consistent across the piece, white space as the highlight, no outline characters at the edge of a shaded region (the tone change is the edge). Vertical gradients need fewer rows than horizontal ones need columns.

Texture conventions: foliage % & 8 o O in clumps; fur , ' ; " along a curve; water ~ and ^ alternating; scales (((( or ))))) or =}}}; brick and mesh # + H %; wood | ! ; : vertical runs; metal = - runs with | rivets. Solid fill: # @ 8 M W; use g b d p q at the edge of a solid for a softer edge.

Scenes

Ground line first, across the full width. Draw far layers first, near objects overwrite them. Repeat a unit with small variations for crowds, forests, streets (stagger heights). Near is bigger and heavier; far is smaller and lighter. One prop can carry the story (speech bubble, zzZ, \*, a moon). Captions and the artist tag can be composed into the scene, aligned with a feature.

Converting an image description to text

If asked to render a described photo or image: reduce to a tonal map, sample at a 1:2 cell ratio, map through the weight ramp (dark characters for dark tones on a light background; reverse for a dark terminal), then hand place the focal features, especially eyes. Prefer simple subjects, tight crops, no busy background. Say plainly that detail is limited by cell size and ask whether the user wants a larger or a Unicode (block or Braille) version, which is sharper but font dependent.

Animation

If asked for animation, produce a list of frames, all the same width and height, changing as few cells as possible between frames, holding key poses for more than one frame, and state the intended frame rate. For terminal use, provide a clear and redraw loop rather than escape codes unless asked.

Unicode, if the user wants it

Box drawing ─ │ ┌ ┐ └ ┘ ├ ┤ ┬ ┴ ┼ ═ ║ ╔ ╗ ╚ ╝, block elements █ ▓ ▒ ░ ▀ ▄ ▌ ▐, Braille ⠁ through ⣿ (2 by 4 dots per cell). Label the result as Unicode art and warn that it needs a font with those glyphs at monospace width.

Delivering

Present the art in a text code block. Add at most one short line of context. If the user will paste it somewhere with unknown fonts (email, chat), warn that it needs a monospace font and offer a smaller, font tolerant version. If the piece is wider than 72 columns, say so.

Self check before sending (run every time)
Only printable ASCII (or requested Unicode), no tabs.
No line over the width limit; count the longest line.
Symmetric features on matching columns; frames closed; all frame rows equal width.
Strokes continuous cell to cell; curves stepped one row at a time.
Silhouette readable with the features covered.
Original, or credited with initials intact.
